To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the levels of GnRHR and GnRH were lower in the hypothalamo-pituitary complex of anoestrous sheep in comparison with those of animals in the luteal and/or follicular phases of oestrous cycle, and (ii) these differences were reflected by the changes in plasma LH level.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach to the understanding of the mechanisms regulating the biosynthesis of GnRH and the GnRHR in sheep during anoestrus and cyclic phases of the reproductive cycle.
the elucidation of the mechanisms of the regulation of the hypothalamic GnRH biosynthesis in the hypothalami-pituitary axis of ewes during anoestrus and cyclic phases of the oestrus cycle.
the molecular mechanisms of GnRH and its receptor biosynthesis in the hypothalmo-pituitary system of anoestrous animals and the relationship with plasma LH concentrations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GnRH and GnRH receptor levels in the hypothalamo-pituitary axis are not always associated with LH secretion in sheep.
the GnRHa-induced LH secretion in sheep is not only due to an increase in GnRH biosynthesis, but also to a higher GnRHR expression in the hypothalami-pituitary axis.
the GnRH biosynthesis in the hypothalamo-hypophysial unit in sheep during anoestrus is lower than in cyclic animals and that the GnRHH biosynthesis is lower than in luteally active animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

GnRH and GnRH receptor are involved in regulation of LH secretion during the reproductive cycle in sheep, but their expression and function are not always related to the oestrous phase of the reproductive cycle.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the hypothalamic GnRH and pituitary GnRHR are involved in the control of the LH secretion during the anoestrus period and the follicular and luteal phases of the oestrus cycle in sheep.
the GnRHA/GnRHR system is a key regulator of LH secretion in the ewe, and that the hypothalamus-pituitary axis is an important site for regulation of GnRH biosynthesis and GnRHR expression in sheep.
the GnRH and GnRH receptor expression in the hypothalami of anoestrous animals is lower than that detected during the follicular and luteal phases of the oestrus cycle.
